thread.title: Riley County Police report arrests and case summaries for May 5
thread.title_full: Riley County Police report arrests and case summaries for May 5

author: Sunflower State News
title: Riley County Police report arrests and case summaries for May 5
text:
The Riley County Police Department announced on May 6 that two individuals were arrested in Manhattan as part of its ongoing efforts to provide transparency through daily reports. The agency said it withholds some details to protect community members and comply with laws.
According to the department, Isabella Jean Counts, age 21, was arrested at approximately 10:27 p.m. on May 5 in the 900 block of Moro Street on a Riley County District Court warrant for failure to appear. The original charges include criminal deprivation of property, criminal deprivation of a motor vehicle, unlawful acts concerning computers, and criminal damage to property. Counts received a total bond of $10,000 and is no longer confined in the Riley County Jail.
Antuan Devon Smith, age 18, was arrested at approximately 11:20 a.m. on May 5 in the 300 block of Denison Avenue for aggravated robbery and trafficking contraband into a correctional facility. The arrest stems from an initial report filed on July 25. Smith was issued a $50,000 bond and remains confined at the time of this report.
The police department said that information about calls for service and reports is collected during each twenty-four-hour period from six o’clock in the morning one day until six o’clock the next morning; weekend reports are compiled from Friday at six o’clock in the morning until Monday at six o’clock in the morning. Some names or details may be withheld according to local, state, or federal law.
“Anyone with information about a crime can contact Crime Stoppers. Using Crime Stoppers allows you to remain anonymous and could qualify you for a cash reward of up to $1,000,” said officials from the Riley County Police Department.
For more information or details about employment opportunities within the department or further clarification regarding their release policies, readers are directed by police officials to visit their Media Guide or Employment Page.
